chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn al-Sindi, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The Friday prayer is obligatory upon the one who is within two farsakhs of it.

key_terms.فَرْسَخَيْنِ: Two farsakhs (a traditional unit of distance)

ai.seo_question: What is the maximum distance for the Friday prayer to be obligatory according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith, transmitted through the chain of Zurarah and Muhammad ibn Muslim, establishes the legal threshold for the obligation of Friday prayer based on proximity to the congregation. In Shia jurisprudence, this distance of two farsakhs (approximately 12 kilometers) defines the boundary for those who must attend the communal prayer rather than performing Dhuhr individually, reflecting the practical considerations of early Islamic community life.
